the role of growth factors in follicular development, and in particular, with the role of the EGF family of growth factors in the ovulatory process.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EGF-related growth factor family members amphireguin, epiregulins, and betacellulin are paracrine LH mediators of cumulus cell expansion and oocyte meiotic maturation.
EGF-like growth factors are parakrine mediators that amplify the LH signal throughout follicle.
LH stimulates a cascade of EGF-like growth factors, which are responsible for the follicular events that culminate in ovulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EGF family mediates the action of LH in the ovulating follicle.
LH induces a cascade of EGF-like growth factors that are secreted by granulosa cells, and that these factors act in a paracrine manner to mediate the LH action on cumulus expansion and ovulation.
EGF-related growth factor expression in the ovulatory follicle is induced by LH and that these factors are essential for ovulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LH signal can be amplified by EGF-like growth factors to induce the morphological changes necessary for ovulation.
LH stimulates the expression of EGF family members, which in turn mediate LH action on the cumulus cells.
LH action in the follicle is not restricted to the theca and granulosa cells but is propagated by EGF family members to the oocyte, cumulus cells, and mural granulosa cells.
